script.title: Why Mars Rovers Must Drive Themselves Across the Red Planet
script.description: Because radio signals can take up to twenty-two minutes to reach Mars, rovers must use onboard artificial intelligence to navigate the surface safely.

shots.narration: From hundreds of millions of kilometers away, scientists send daily instructions to the Perseverance rover, steering our robotic presence across an ancient Martian lakebed.
Even when Earth and Mars line up at their closest approach, radio signals traveling at the speed of light still take three full minutes to bridge the gap.
When the planets drift to opposite sides of the sun, that delay stretches to twenty two minutes, forcing the rover to evaluate terrain and steer itself safely.
